encoding: Two free booleans e=os.path.exists(resultsFileName), f=globalParameters[ForceRedoBenchmarkProblems]; predicate = Or(Not(e), f). Pure boolean disjunction within the harvested op-surface (Or/Not); no arithmetic/compare/subscript-of-runtime needed once the two operands are abstracted to the seeded booleans.

true_examples.meaning: results CSV does not exist and ForceRedo off -> guard True -> runClient executes (benchmark runs because no prior results)
results CSV exists but ForceRedoBenchmarkProblems=True (the hardcoded default) -> guard True -> benchmark reruns regardless of cached CSV

false_examples.meaning: UNIQUE false assignment: results CSV already present AND ForceRedo disabled -> guard False -> takes else branch print1("# Already benchmarked; skipping.")

crosshair.caveat: CrossHair: absence of counterexample is NOT a proof. The authoritative proof is the z3 exhaustive 4-row truth table above (all assignments enumerated over the finite bool x bool domain).

assumptions: os.path.exists(resultsFileName) is abstracted to a free boolean per the seeded domain. In live execution it is a filesystem syscall on resultsFileName = OutputPath/1_BenchmarkProblems/<groupName>/<stepName>/../Data/<stepName>.csv (derived from CLI OutputPath + YAML BenchmarkProblems config). The boolean disjunction itself is fully static once that operand is fixed.

globalParameters[ForceRedoBenchmarkProblems] is a YAML/CLI-controlled bool (hardcoded default True). To even reach a False predicate it must be set False via YAML GlobalParameters or --global-parameters; otherwise the guard is unconditionally True and the benchmark always reruns.
